narrative.overview:
Every session is a strip in a bay, racked by what it needs from you. The developer runs many Pi and Claude Code sessions at once, keyboard first, for long stretches at a desk. The window answers one question before any other: which sessions need me? A 344px bay on the left holds every session as a fixed-height strip, sorted into Needs you, Running and Settled. The open session fills the centre. A 304px workspace column on the right shows its changes, branch and terminal.

The system is Eldritch at shell scale: a blue-slate ground, the bay one tonal step above it, and green spent only where it means something. The surfaces are flat. Depth comes from tone, and shadows belong to overlays. Density is high and regular: one 8px construction grid sets every strip, column and gutter, and every list of live things shares one strip shape, so fields line up on one baseline across the bay, tool calls, changed files, terminals and resources.

The world refuses two things by name: the three-pane IDE (file tree left, tabbed editor, bottom panel) and the chat app (bubbles, the agent drawn as a person). Transcript prose sits in a 75ch column, tool calls render as inline strips, and a permission request is the focal point of the view.
keyCharacteristics: Sessions racked by attention, with Needs you as the only lifted green band
Fixed-height strips with the same fields on one baseline in every list
Flat tonal layers on an 8px grid, with shadows only on overlays
Overpass at a fixed scale with cap-centred controls, Overpass Mono for paths, numbers and durations
Green on what needs you and on one primary action per surface, cyan on focus only

rules.name: The Needs You Rule
rules.body: Green means the developer is needed. It appears on what waits for them and on the one primary action a surface allows, such as Save, Start a session or Allow once. A second green element on a surface is a defect.

rules.name: The Marks Only Rule
rules.body: State colours live on marks and state lines, never on fills, row backgrounds or titles. Every mark pairs its colour with a shape (filled dot, spinning ring, dashed ring, diamond, square) and a text label.

rules.name: The Cyan Is Focus Rule
rules.body: Cyan draws the focus ring, the caret and the selection wash. Selection of a row or tab is neutral: the selected surface plus a control-strength ring.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: A surface picks one of the roles above and never a size of its own. No text goes below 12px except the uppercase section label and key caps (11px).

rules.name: The Cap-Centring Rule
rules.body: Every single-line label in a control or row sits in its own element, and that element trims its box to the cap height and the baseline (`text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic`). Flex centring then lines the capitals up with icons and marks. Where `text-box` is missing, the label moves down by the measured Overpass offset (0.11em). A label that truncates gives its descenders back as 6px block padding and takes the same space back as negative margin, so its centre does not move.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Mono marks something the machine owns: a path, a command, a number, a duration. It is never decoration.

rules.name: The One Grid Rule
rules.body: Every strip, column and gutter lands on the 8px grid. A value off the grid needs a measured reason, such as the 6px descender padding.

rules.name: The 32px Control Rule
rules.body: Every button, field, picker and select is 32px tall with 14px text, in toolbars, rows, notices, cards and banners alike. A container that holds a button is at least 40px tall.

rules.name: The Shadows Cover Rule
rules.body: A shadow means something covers other content. Resting surfaces never carry one.

rules.name: The Attention Rack Rule
rules.body: The bay racks strips by what they need, and only Needs you holds full voice. Running and Settled recede through colour and weight, never through opacity, so their text keeps AA contrast on the bay.

dos: **Do** put every list of live things in strips: 56px two-line or 32px one-line, lead, main, meta.
**Do** keep Needs you as the only lifted, green-headed section in the bay.
**Do** make every control 32px tall, including buttons in notices, cards and banners.
**Do** centre labels on their capitals with a trimmed text box.
**Do** set paths, commands, counts and durations in Overpass Mono with ligatures off.
**Do** pair every state colour with a mark shape and a text label.
**Do** break long paths after a slash and long identifiers at `::` and `_`.
donts: **Don't** use green for anything beyond what waits on the developer and the surface's one primary action.
**Don't** fill rows, titles or backgrounds with state colours.
**Don't** recede text with opacity. Use Mist and a lighter weight.
**Don't** put a shadow on a resting surface.
**Don't** add a second authored motion, or animate the transcript or the terminal canvas.
**Don't** draw the agent as a person or the transcript as chat bubbles.
**Don't** add editor boilerplate such as encoding, line endings or indent to the status bar. It shows only the cursor position and the save state.
